title: Solar Polar Brightening and Radius at 100 and 230 GHz Observed by ALMA
question: Is polar brightening present in ALMA single-dish solar maps at 100 and 230 GHz, how large is it, and how does it (and the solar radius) compare with the FAL-C and SSC atmospheric models?

data.bands: Band 3 (84-116 GHz), six maps; Band 6 (211-275 GHz), three maps; reference 100 and 230 GHz

what.value: Quiet-Sun brightness temperatures 7280±250 K (100 GHz) and 5900±190 K (230 GHz) for comparison

evidence.quote: in agreement with the values suggested by (cite: White2017) ($7280\pm250$ K)
suggested that the observations were best fitted by the average quiet Sun model C (FAL-C) proposed by (cite: FAL1993).

what.value: SSC atmospheric model with extended chromosphere

evidence.quote: The observed polar brightenings were also compared with atmospheric model SSC proposed by (cite: Selhorst2005a)
we combine the historical data compiled by (cite: Rozelot2015) and (cite: Menezes2017)

recipe.method: Convolve with Gaussian of 54" from theta100^2=theta230^2+theta_x^2
Average of 61 radial profiles every 1 deg at PA 60-120 (South) and 240-300 (North); peak relative to T_qS
Contour at 0.5 T_qS, 1440 points, circle fit
Compute Tb from FAL-C and SSC with H and H- free-free opacities, 2D expansion with R=696 Mm, Gaussian convolution to 25" and 58"
